entry.title: MLB: What to watch on August 24, 2026
entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

Ashcraft's electric arm makes this one worth your evening even if Robbie Ray's presence gives you pause. The Pirates' 26-year-old righty enters riding a stretch that got him an All-Star nod as a Misiorowski injury replacement, and he's been nails lately — he beat the Tigers his last time out, allowing one run on five hits while striking out four across eight innings without a walk. His 11.81 pNERD, built on elite strike-throwing and 97-mph heat, is the best pitching mark in today's slate. Ray, by contrast, is scuffling — his below-average strikeout stuff and wandering command produce a middling xFIP and the lowest pNERD on the board, though he's avoided disaster results so far. San Diego brings the juice on the other side of the ball: the Padres have won 14 of their last 18 games and sit tied for the final NL wild card spot, while Pittsburgh has dropped three straight and needs to find something on the road. The Padres' bullpen (headlined by a lights-out closer) and strong glovework push their tNERD near the top of today's games, giving this one a 14.50 gNERD that clears the historical 95th percentile.

Boston Red Sox @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

Boston's high-flying offense meets a hot Sandy Alcantara at loanDepot Park, and the tNERD numbers say the "middling" Marlins deserve more respect than their record suggests. Miami actually posts the higher team score here thanks to a young, cheap roster and standout baserunning, while positive luck marks for both sides hint they've been slightly better than their run differentials show. Alcantara has quietly rounded into form — he's averaged roughly 6.54 innings per start this season, and 20.3 outs over his last 15 — and his pNERD gets a real lift from mid-90s-plus velocity that grades near the top of the league. Suarez brings a strong xFIP- and a deliberate pace that plays well on TV, though he's on six days rest after a shaky outing against Arizona where he allowed four earned runs over 5⅓ innings. Notably, Suarez owns a 7-2 record with a 3.07 ERA in 22 career appearances against Miami, giving this some built-in familiarity. With a gNERD of 13.85, comfortably above the day's 11.15 average and solidly in the upper tier historically, this is a legitimately watchable pitching-forward matchup rather than the mismatch the moneyline implies.

Chicago Cubs @ Arizona Diamondbacks, 6:40p

Summary

The Cubs bring the NL's best offense to the desert, and Merrill Kelly is the pitcher standing in its way — that's the whole ballgame in one sentence, and it favors turning this one on. Chicago, fresh off a 19-2 blowout of Seattle, arrives with a comfortable wild-card cushion while Arizona sits just outside the field, making every game in this series matter for the Diamondbacks even if it's mostly background noise for the Cubs. Kelly comes in reeling — he gave up six earned runs and allowed seven hits in four innings against the Red Sox — and his 1.56 pNERD reflects an xFIP- north of 120, ugly even by contact-manager standards. Gausman, since being acquired from the Toronto Blue Jays at the trade deadline, is unlucky more than bad — his 6.55 pNERD is buoyed by strong swinging-strike and strike-rate marks plus a healthy luck bump, suggesting better results are coming. The Cubs' 10.66 tNERD is elite, driven by standout fielding and a Pete Crow-Armstrong-powered lineup, while Arizona's offense and broadcast appeal lag. At 12.10, this gNERD sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — worth a look, particularly for Cubs fans and Kelly's opponents alike.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Seattle Mariners, 6:40p

Summary

I have enough to work with now.

Two aces, one pitcher's park, and a real reason to tune in. Zack Wheeler and Logan Gilbert headline this one, and both bring legitimate strikeout stuff into T-Mobile Park, a venue built to smother offense. Kyle Schwarber has been a wrecking ball all season with 39 home runs, while Zack Wheeler's 2.92 ERA makes him one of the more difficult pitchers in the league to solve. Wheeler's peripherals back that up — his xFIP- sits at an excellent 70, and his elite whiff rate drives a pNERD score comfortably above today's average. Gilbert isn't far behind, pairing a 96 mph fastball with strong swing-and-miss numbers, though his plodding pace docks him slightly. Wheeler has 144 strikeouts in 120.1 innings, a 10.8 K/9 rate, so expect quick outs and quiet innings from both dugouts.

The team scores tell a lopsider story, though: Philadelphia's bullpen depth and baserunning give it a solid tNERD, while Seattle's shaky defense drags its number down near replacement level. At 35-30 at home, T-Mobile Park has been a genuine advantage for the Mariners, so don't assume the visitors coast. With a gNERD of 11.89 — above both the historical and today's averages — this game earns its slot on the watch list primarily through pitching craft rather than offensive fireworks; go in expecting a tense, low-scoring affair rather than a slugfest.

Cincinnati Reds @ San Francisco Giants, 6:45p

Summary

Chase Burns is the reason to tune in here, even if everything else about this game is fighting an uphill battle. The 23-year-old righty is running a 97.7 mph fastball with elite swing-and-miss stuff (xFIP- of 83), and his 10.10 pNERD is comfortably above today's average, making him the single most watchable thing on either roster. Everything else, though, is muted: combined tNERD of 4.04 is well below the historical midpoint, reflecting two teams playing out the string — the Reds are road favorites at -140 over a Giants team that has faded badly and now leans on pitching and ballpark to keep games close. San Francisco's lineup still has some juice via Jung Hoo Lee, hitting .289 with 9 home runs and 46 RBI, and Casey Schmitt, who has quietly put together 21 home runs and 55 RBI, while Elly De La Cruz gives the Reds a disruptive presence atop the order with 76 runs scored and 22 stolen bases. The Giants' opponent is a TBD arm with zero pNERD data, so this is essentially Burns-or-bust for entertainment value — a 11.59 gNERD that's solid but not special, propped up almost entirely by one electric rookie arm.

Texas Rangers @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

A playoff-race game with middling pitching but a White Sox lineup that's quietly become worth watching. Texas arrives in Chicago in the thick of it—tied atop the AL West and fighting for a wild-card spot—while the White Sox sit atop the AL Central at 68-62, so there's real stakes even if the pitching matchup doesn't scream must-see. Kumar Rocker's pNERD of 3.79 reflects a season that's been more grind than dominance—he's 4-10 with a 4.46 ERA and 109 strikeouts in 121 innings—with shaky command dragging things down even as his strikeout stuff and youth help. Chicago's probable, Jose Urquidy, has no pNERD data available, so consider his half of the mound a mystery box. The real juice here is the White Sox offense: young, cheap, and hitting the ball hard, with a tNERD of 8.54 built on strong batting runs, an elite barrel rate, and a bullpen that's quietly been effective. Texas, by contrast, is merely fine at 5.27, buoyed mostly by a well-above-average luck score suggesting some positive regression could be coming. Overall gNERD of 11.30 lands a shade above the historic average—decent, not electric.

Tampa Bay Rays @ Detroit Tigers, 3:40p

Summary

Interesting to note: Framber Valdez is now with the Tigers (not Astros anymore), which I should incorporate. Now let me write the summary.

Skip this one unless you're specifically chasing the AL East leader's road trip or morbid curiosity about a former World Series ace scuffling in a new uniform. Drew Rasmussen brings real stuff to the mound—his xFIP- of 77 and 8.30 pNERD are legit top-shelf, and he's punched out at least five batters in 17 of 24 starts this year—but he's also coming off a rough turn against Toronto where he gave up five runs on seven hits while striking out five over five frames to take the loss in a 7-6 final. On the other side, Framber Valdez—now a Tiger after years in Houston—has been genuinely bad lately: over his last 11⅓ innings he's posted a 6.35 ERA and 5.47 FIP, walking nine and allowing 11 hits, numbers his 3.10 pNERD reflects. Detroit is limping into this one too, aiming to break a five-game skid, while Tampa Bay owns the highest team batting average in the AL at .261. The Rays' offense and Rasmussen's whiffs give this some appeal, but Detroit's tNERD (4.04) and Valdez's shaky command drag the gNERD (10.30) to just below average compared to today's slate (avg. 11.15) and historical norms (mean 10.81).

Colorado Rockies @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

I have enough information to write the summary.

Cade Cavalli is quietly having a breakout season, and he's the entire reason to tune in to this one. The rest of the game—two last-place-adjacent clubs sputtering toward September—is not doing you many favors.

Cavalli, still just three years removed from Tommy John surgery, has been one of the more effective arms in the league lately: he's sitting at 5-7, 5.97... RHP Cade Cavalli (11-5, 3.22) with a 96.6 mph fastball and a tidy 77 xFIP-, both of which power his 7.59 pNERD—comfortably above today's average. Feltner, by contrast, owns 5.97 ERA, 1.52 WHIP, 64 strikeouts and an xFIP- north of 120, translating to a below-replacement 2.16 pNERD; he's simply overmatched here. On the team side, Washington's tNERD (9.04) dwarfs Colorado's anemic 0.62, thanks to a younger, faster, more athletic Nationals lineup, though their bullpen has been a mess and they've dropped six of their last seven games and have struggled to score consistently. Colorado, meanwhile, is without Hunter Goodman, who lands on the injury report with a shoulder issue, further thinning an already bottom-of-the-league offense. At 9.70, the gNERD lands below the historical and today's averages—watch for Cavalli, not much else.

Cleveland Guardians @ Los Angeles Angels, 6:38p

Summary

Guardians pitcher rookie of year candidate, Klassen also rookie. Angels team stats poor. Let's write summary.

A rookie pitching showcase wrapped in a mostly lopsided, low-stakes affair. Cleveland's Parker Messick, quietly one of the AL's best first-year arms, headlines a game that's more about individual craft than team drama, since the Angels' offense and defense have been a season-long mess.

Messick, who has emerged as a top three choice for AL Rookie of the Year with a 2.54 ERA that ranks 7th in the majors and 152 strikeouts, comes in fresh off a strong outing where he went 6 2/3 innings against the Giants, surrendering just one earned run. His 8.33 pNERD is well above average for today's slate, built on a stingy xFIP-, a quick pace, and rookie youth. Opposite him is Angels rookie George Klassen, who touches 96.5 mph but pairs it with shaky command — his low strike rate and inflated xFIP- drag his pNERD down to 2.58, a mismatch reflected in the 9-8 Messick vs. 2-1 Klassen ledgers. The Guardians own a healthy 7.26 tNERD thanks to strong baserunning, fielding, and a low payroll/young roster, while the Angels' offense and defense (both well below average) sink their tNERD to a paltry 1.19. Overall gNERD of 9.68 sits a bit below the historic median and today's average — watchable for the Messick start, skippable otherwise.

New York Mets @ Chicago White Sox, 11:10a

Summary

I'll proceed with the information gathered from the successful searches.

A rookie sensation with a knee-buckling curveball squares off against a bullpen journeyman having a career revival, on a Chicago South Side surprise team that's quietly become one of baseball's youngest and most fun outfits. This one clears the bar for watchability, and the numbers back up the eyeball test.

Nolan McLean, the Mets' 24-year-old with what scouts already call one of the best curveballs in the league, brings a 7.98 pNERD built on a stingy xFIP- and electric stuff. He had his worst start of the season last time out, surrendering five earned runs over five innings, though he's still pitched to a 3.42 ERA in 24 starts this season. After his midseason call-up to the majors last year, he lit up stuff models en route to a sparkling ERA and WHIP, sitting mid-90s with two fastballs and a curveball that grades as one of the best in the game. Across the mound, Sean Newcomb isn't a household name but posts a respectable 5.61 pNERD, helped by a fast pace and solid contact management, even while absorbing some rough puck. The White Sox, sporting the league's youngest roster and a payroll near the bottom of MLB, still have out-produced expectations at the plate, giving this game a tNERD of 8.74 that dwarfs the Mets' 5.43. With a gNERD of 13.88, well above the historical average and near the top of today's slate, this is one worth carving out time for.

Cristopher Sánchez is having the kind of season that makes an ace's Sunday start must-watch, and this rubber-adjacent finale between two teams still fighting for playoff positioning gives it real stakes on top of the pitching. Sánchez brings a 10.09 pNERD — well above today's average — built on a strikeout-heavy, ground-ball profile that's produced a sparkling xFIP- of 61 and elite swinging-strike and strike rates; he's compiled a 2.51 ERA with 187 strikeouts and has allowed one earned run or fewer in three of his last four starts. Leahy is a serviceable middle-of-the-pack arm (5.42 pNERD) with a strong xFIP- of 88 but low whiff numbers, and he'll need to keep the ball down against a Phillies lineup fueled by Schwarber's MLB-leading power. The Little League Classic gives this one a fun backdrop, and the Brewers' NL-best roster gives it real substance too. Milwaukee brings the majors' most well-rounded lineup to Williamsport, and their 10.03 tNERD - built on strong baserunning, a deep bullpen, and a young, cost-effective roster - ranks near the top of today's slate. Atlanta, by contrast, is a middling 5.08 tNERD outfit still shaking off a rough season, though a hefty barrel rate suggests some thump in the lineup once the puck-luck evens out; Atlanta's batting and baserunning numbers are actually underperforming their skill level, hinting at better days ahead.

On the mound, it's a matchup of newcomers: Mahle was acquired by the Braves at the trade deadline in a deal with the Giants, his fifth team in a decade of ball. His 5.18 pNERD is respectable, buoyed almost entirely by tough luck - his peripherals suggest he deserves better than his ERA shows. Add it up and you get a 13.37 gNERD, comfortably above both the season's median and today's average - a legitimately watchable game featuring exactly the kind of stage MLB likes to put in a Little League ballpark.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 4:15p

Summary

This is the best-looking matchup on the board today, full stop. With a gNERD of 18.64 sitting right at the top of today's slate (today's games range from 4.26 to 18.64) and creeping toward the historic ceiling of 20.20, this Pirates-Dodgers tilt pairs two hard-throwing arms with two lineups that can actually hit.

Tarik Skubal takes the ball for LA sporting the best pitcher score of anyone playing today (11.90), built on a microscopic 65 xFIP-, elite swinging-strike and strike rates, and mid-90s-plus stuff that simply doesn't allow hard contact. On the other side, Jared Jones brings his own well-earned intrigue: he returned from internal brace surgery on his UCL, and the images coming back negative meant he'd avoided a serious injury after getting drilled by a comebacker mid-start. His surface numbers have been rocky since returning, a 5.75 ERA over 20.1 innings with a 1.52 WHIP, but his 98.3 mph average velocity and strong peripherals suggest better days are ahead, and his positive luck score backs that up. The Dodgers' loaded offense (tNERD 8.48) against a scrappy, athletic Pirates club that runs well and gets solid bullpen work rounds out a genuinely well-built game worth carving out time for.

Washington Nationals @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

Miami's Eury Pérez is must-watch stuff, even if the standings around him mean nothing. The 23-year-old right-hander carries a 15-inning scoreless streak into this one and has been Miami's best story of August, posting a 2.00 ERA through three starts this month, backed by 98 mph heat and elite swing-and-miss stuff that gives him the day's best pNERD score by a mile. Jake Irvin, by contrast, is scuffling — a 2-7 record with a 5.80 ERA and an xFIP- that agrees he's been more hittable than lucky, though positive luck does suggest some correction is overdue. Neither the Nationals (61-69) nor Marlins (65-64) are playing for much beyond pride, but both rosters skew young and cheap, which the tNERD model loves — low payrolls, low ages, and Washington's excellent baserunning and barrel rates offset a genuinely miserable bullpen. Miami's own offense is unspectacular but has overperformed its skills all year. CJ Abrams, already banged up, has historically been overmatched against Pérez. With a gNERD near the top of today's slate, this is one where the pitching matchup carries the appeal even if the standings don't.

Atlanta Braves @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Logan Henderson pitching against a contending Braves lineup is reason enough to tune in, with a scuffling Martín Pérez along for the ride making this look more like a mismatch than a marquee duel. Henderson has been one of the better stories in Milwaukee's rotation this year, and he carries a 2.70 ERA and 3.39 FIP with 75 strikeouts across 63 1/3 innings, having been fantastic in his last outing against the Dodgers, tossing a career-high seven frames on a career-high 93 pitches, allowing one run on three hits and a walk, striking out six. It's also his first career start against Atlanta. His 9.71 pNERD, built on a sharp xFIP- and strong strike-throwing, dwarfs Pérez's modest 3.37, which reflects diminished velocity and shaky command from the 35-year-old journeyman now with his seventh organization. Milwaukee's tNERD of 10.15 stands out too, fueled by a young, athletic roster, quality baserunning, and a deep bullpen. Combine that with Atlanta's respectable 5.43 team mark and you get a gNERD of 14.33, comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — a good bet if you like watching a rising young arm work against a lineup still trying to solve him.

McClanahan is the headliner here, freshly activated off the injured list after a bout of back tightness and still working back up to a full workload following a rehab stint, but when healthy he's been legitimately excellent — a 3.09-ish xFIP-driven profile with mid-90s velocity and a quick pace that helped push his pNERD to 6.26, comfortably above average. Brandon Young, by contrast, offers modest intrigue as a still-developing arm whose surface numbers (9-3 record) outpace his so-so xFIP-. Tampa's offense has real thump from Junior Caminero, and its team metrics suggest they've been underperforming their skill level and could be due for better results, while Baltimore's barrel rate and bullpen depth round out a competent, if unspectacular, roster. With a gNERD of 10.54, this sits almost exactly at the historical median — worth a look mainly for McClanahan's return, not appointment viewing otherwise.

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ Milwaukee Brewers, 1:10p

Summary

This one has it all: two of the best pitchers in baseball, a real division-race stake, and a preview of a potential October rematch. The gNERD of 20.64 is the top mark of today's slate and among the highest scores in the dataset's history, and once you see the details, it's not hard to see why.

Misiorowski is the headline act, sporting a pNERD of 15.87 that leads the league today, built on a triple-digit fastball (100.7 mph average), a filthy swinging-strike rate, and an xFIP- of 48 that's simply absurd. He's overmatching opponents with a 100-plus mph fastball and a knee-buckling cutter, compiling a big-league-high 210 strikeouts. Across the mound, 37-year-old Sale is no slouch either, still pumping mid-90s heat with elite command, good for a 9.84 pNERD. The pitchers with the major leagues' top two ERAs will go head to head as the NL East-leading Atlanta Braves visit Jacob Misiorowski and the NL Central-leading Milwaukee Brewers, with some suggesting it's quite possibly a pitching preview of Game 1 of an NL Division Series matchup. The Brewers' tNERD of 10.14 is buoyed by strong baserunning and bullpen work, giving this one both star power and team quality — a rare slate-topper worth clearing your schedule for.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Washington Nationals @ Texas Rangers, 5:05p

Summary

Jacob deGrom takes the mound with genuine intrigue attached: this is a pitcher trying to prove his triceps and hip are cooperating after exiting a start against the Angels a week ago having thrown just two innings before shutting it down. If he's right, watch closely — his stuff still ticks every analytical box, with a 97.3 mph fastball, elite swinging-strike rate, and an xFIP- of 76 that would make pitchers half his age jealous, driving a pNERD of 10.78, comfortably above the day's average. The oft-injured deGrom has a chance to match last season's total of 30 starts, the first time he had reached that number since making 32 in each of his Cy Young Award seasons with the New York Mets in 2018-19. Opposite him, Andrew Alvarez is a perfectly serviceable lefty (pNERD 5.08) without much sizzle — think of him as the seasoning rather than the main course. The Nationals bring real offensive juice, with strong barrel rates and baserunning value pushing their tNERD to 9.17, though a shaky bullpen keeps dragging on their ceiling. The Rangers, by contrast, are a middling, slightly unlucky team (tNERD 4.97) that's gone 3-7 over their last ten. With a gNERD of 15.00 — well above both the historical and today's averages — this one earns its spot near the top of the watch list, deGrom health permitting.

San Francisco Giants @ Cleveland Guardians, 10:10a

Summary

Gavin Williams is having a quietly dominant season, and this is your best excuse of the day to watch a last-place team's road trip. The gNERD score of 14.71 sits comfortably above both the historic 95th percentile (15.60) and today's slate average of 10.50, driven almost entirely by Williams' excellent stuff on the mound.

Williams brings 190 strikeouts and 11 wins, making him one of the more quietly effective starters in the American League, backed by a filthy 70 xFIP- and 97.2 mph average velocity that produce his 12.17 pNERD — comfortably above the 95th percentile line of 10.50. He did get roughed up last time out, allowing five runs in 4 1/3 innings against San Diego, so there's some risk of an early hook. Roupp is respectable if unspectacular (5.54 pNERD), with an 86.3 mph average exit velocity, 29.9% hard-hit rate and 5.1% barrel rate undercut by control issues that have limited him to 5.1 innings per start. On the team side, Cleveland's 7.63 tNERD outpaces San Francisco's 4.09, fueled by a young, cheap roster and a bullpen that's been quietly excellent all year. Neither offense is scary, but with Williams dealing, this one's worth a look.

Seattle Mariners @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Milwaukee, sitting comfortably atop the NL Central at 78-48, hosts a Mariners club (59-67) whose offense is basically a museum exhibit on how not to score runs — worth tuning in mostly to watch a good team beat up on a bad one, but there's enough pitching intrigue to justify the watch. George Kirby brings the swing-and-miss stuff you want from an ace, sitting at nearly 97 mph with excellent strike-throwing and a tidy xFIP-, and he owns the highest pNERD in this matchup by a clear margin. Robert Gasser, a former Brewer prospect who debuted back in 2024, counters with solid strike-throwing of his own but middling stuff, netting a more modest pNERD. Seattle's offense has been the team's biggest weakness this season, averaging just 3.9 runs per game, 30th in MLB, with a .229 average and .377 slugging — grim reading for Mariners fans. Milwaukee's tNERD of 9.88 is well above the historical 95th percentile, fueled by strong baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young, affordable roster, while Seattle's 3.02 mark reflects real flaws in fielding and baserunning that its offense-only luck (positive, meaning some regression upward may be coming) hasn't offset yet. With a gNERD of 12.51, this sits comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — not a marquee event, but a legitimately watchable pitching duel wrapped around a lopsided team quality gap.

Seymour is the real story here: a converted reliever now stretching out as a starter, he posts a strong 7.70 pNERD thanks to a tidy xFIP-, and he's 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA in three August starts, striking out nine over six innings in his last outing. Tampa's tNERD (5.92) also gets a lift from positive batting and baserunning value plus some positive regression looming. Toronto's low barrel rate and batting runs drag their tNERD down to 2.52. Detail

Chicago White Sox @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

A high-scoring Crosstown Classic finale with real playoff stakes for both sides — this one's worth your remote. With a 14.78 gNERD, this White Sox-Cubs series capper ranks near the top of today's slate and comfortably above the historical average, driven mostly by the Cubs' excellent 10.04 tNERD, fueled by a Sox offense driven by the home run ball, with a lineup built around three sluggers who each have over 25 homers facing off against a Cubs team boasting standout batting and fielding runs. It's worth noting it's rare when both Chicago baseball teams are on track to make the playoffs in August, which gives this series some extra juice. On the mound, Sean Newcomb has been effective out of the White Sox pen and now starts, holding right-handed hitters to just a .194 average this season after tossing 2 1/3 hitless innings against Detroit on Sunday, while Clay Holmes brings a solid xFIP-based pNERD of his own. Neither arm is elite by pNERD standards, but both grade out useful, and the offense-forward Cubs lineup should keep this one lively.

Detroit Tigers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 9:35a

Summary

Paul Skenes remains appointment viewing even when he's not at his absolute best, and that's the whole case for this one. The reigning NL Cy Young winner enters with a pedestrian-for-him 3.88 ERA and has scuffled since late July — a 6.52 ERA over his last four starts, with 20 hits and 11 walks in 19⅓ innings against the Cubs, Reds, Brewers and Marlins — but the underlying stuff hasn't gone anywhere, and his 10.71 pNERD (well above today's 6.05 average) reflects an elite xFIP-, mid-90s velocity, and a whiff rate that still misses bats. Across the mound, Taj Bradley brings real firepower — a 6.39 pNERD built on mid-90s-plus velocity (his 97.1 mph average grades out well above league norm) and solid strikeout ability, making him one of the more watchable arms on the slate today. Team-wise, Atlanta's 5.51 tNERD outpaces Minnesota's 2.94, with the Braves getting a lift from strong barrel rates and bullpen work, while the Twins are dragged down by shaky fielding and baserunning. The Braves' minus-38 luck figure suggests they've been underperforming and could be due for better results. Overall, a 9.92 gNERD sits a bit below the historic and today's averages — solidly watchable, not essential.

Seattle, by contrast, is a game under .500 and limping in on defense, with a tNERD of just 3.23 dragged down by shaky fielding, though some positive regression (a 19-run luck deficit) could be coming.

The real draw is Kyle Harrison, who's 9-3 with a 2.99 ERA and 3.35 FIP pitching at home, and whose 11.01 pNERD is comfortably above the historic 95th percentile — young, quick-working, and missing bats. Bryce Miller counters with plus velocity and a strong strike rate, giving Seattle a puncher's chance. At 15.34, the gNERD sits near the top of today's slate and well above the historic average, so if you're picking one game, this is a defensible choice.

Jack Perkins gives Oakland a real reason to tune in — a 6.33 pNERD built on mid-90s velocity, a hearty whiff rate, and youth, with the numbers suggesting some positive regression is even in store. His counterpart, reportedly Daniel Lynch IV, arrives as a total mystery on our sheet, no data to speak of. With gNERD sitting at 8.10 — below today's 10.34 average and comfortably below the historic median — this one leans on individual performances rather than aggregate juice.

Chicago White Sox @ Chicago Cubs, 5:05p

Summary

A crosstown rivalry game that actually backs up the hype with two of the day's better team NERD scores. This one sits well above both the historic and today's averages, with the Cubs' 9.70 tNERD anchored by elite team defense and the White Sox punching above their modest payroll thanks to a young, athletic roster.

The Cubs bring MLB's second-best defensive efficiency and fielding runs that rank near the top of the historic distribution, while the White Sox counter with sneaky pop — third in the AL with 164 total home runs, averaging 1.3 per game. It's a Wrigley Field renewal of the crosstown rivalry, with the White Sox riding a 2-game winning streak in the series after taking the last meeting in May. On the mound, Imanaga has been quietly effective (6.04 pNERD, comfortably above average) thanks to excellent whiff and strike rates, though scouts note he's a fly-ball lefty with a 36% ground-ball rate and a 1.8 HR/9 mark — a dangerous combination if the wind cooperates at Wrigley. Castillo, a midseason trade arrival, brings solid stuff (95 mph average velocity) but has been old-fashioned bad-lucky, with a 24.0 luck figure suggesting his results should improve. Between the defense, the power bats, and two capable arms, this is one of the day's most watchable matchups.

Across the diamond, Walker Buehler is scuffling — making his 25th start of the season with a 4.88 ERA in 114⅓ innings pitched, and his 4.46 pNERD is propped up almost entirely by good luck (positive luck score of 21) that says regression is coming, not improvement. The Mets counter with a solid barrel-rate profile but a lineup that's been quietly punchless, not helped by Juan Soto's injured-list absence. At 14.29 gNERD, this sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — worth a look mostly for McLean's arm.

With this being the 11th meeting between these teams this season and the season series tied 5-5, and both clubs jockeying for playoff position, there's context to go with the numbers. Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 1:10p

Summary

Two of the best teams in baseball, a trade-deadline blockbuster reunion, and the two most efficient strikeout-to-walk arms in the league — this is as good as gNERD gets today. Milwaukee and Los Angeles enter this series finale separated by percentage points atop the NL, and the storyline writing itself: the Brewers tried hard to pry Tarik Skubal away from Detroit at the deadline, only to watch the Dodgers land him instead, while Milwaukee kept the guy Detroit reportedly wanted in return — Logan Henderson. Skubal owns the majors' best strikeout-to-walk ratio at 7.11, with Henderson third at 6.27, and both arms grade out as elite by the numbers — Skubal's 11.97 pNERD is driven by a filthy 65 xFIP- and 96.8 mph heat, while Henderson isn't far behind at 9.71, backed by a 71 xFIP- despite still finding his footing in his third career start since returning from a back strain. Both lineups bring thunder too — Henderson has yet to allow more than three runs in any of his 11 starts this season, and Skubal is still looking to settle in after admitting some nerves in his first two starts as a Dodger. With a 19.77 gNERD — comfortably above today's 11.38 average and near the top of the historical range — this is the marquee game of the day.

New York Yankees @ Toronto Blue Jays, 10:37a

Summary

A pitching duel between two legitimately nasty arms is the headline here, even if the offenses around them have gone ice-cold. Dylan Cease brings a 65 xFIP- and a strikeout rate befitting his 191 punchouts this year, and his stuff shows up clearly in the NERD math — 97+ mph heat and elite whiff rates make him the best arm on the board today, with a pNERD near the top of what you'll see all season. Ryan Weathers isn't chopped liver either: he counters at 5-7 with a 3.69 ERA and 136 strikeouts, and was excellent in his last outing, allowing just one earned run over 5.2 innings against Seattle. The lineups, though, are the problem — the Yankees have hit just .202 over their last 27 games, and Toronto isn't much better, with Vladimir Guerrero Jr. out on the 7-day concussion IL and a rotation battered by injuries. Toronto's tNERD is thin thanks to a punchless offense, while New York's barrel-rate and bullpen give them a real team-quality edge. Given the strikeout stuff involved, expect a lot of empty at-bats and a tight, low-scoring finale to the series.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Chicago Cubs, 12:15p

Summary

A slugfest hangover game with real juice: Cardinals prospect Joshua Baez just made history, and Wrigley gets to see if the Cubs can regroup. The Cardinals arrive fresh off St. Louis' 8-4 road win on Saturday, in which the organization's No. 3 prospect, Joshua Baez, became the first player in major league history to hit three home runs in his debut. That's the storyline of the weekend, and it's given the Cardinals a shot at their first time since 2022 that the Cardinals clinched both road series at Chicago. Chicago, meanwhile, is trying to shake off that beating — in a 10-4 start to August, the Cubs have won three consecutive series and seek their fourth in a row.

The gNERD of 13.64 sits comfortably above today's 11.38 average, mostly thanks to the Cubs' tNERD of 9.79 — elite fielding and batting runs make this Chicago lineup genuinely fun, even if the bullpen has been shaky. Edward Cabrera's 6.62 pNERD leans on plus velocity (96.4 mph) and some positive regression coming his way, though his control is spotty. Dobbins, a former Red Sox ACL-tear survivor now in St. Louis via the Willson Contreras trade, brings a tidy modern approach. Worth catching, especially if Baez keeps swinging.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 4:15p

Summary

A dominant ace facing a stacked lineup in a playoff-race showdown—this one's near the top of the watchability charts today, and for good reason. Jacob Misiorowski brings a pNERD of 16.03, comfortably the best mark of any starter today, and the underlying numbers back up the hype: he's MLB's leader in ERA (1.76), strikeouts (204), WHIP (0.74) and opponents' average (.147), riding a fastball that averages 100.6 mph into a Cy Young conversation. His last trip to Dodger Stadium came in relief last October, where he delivered five quality innings in relief with nine strikeouts in Game 3 of last year's NL Championship Series, an outing he now calls the turning point of his season. Across the mound, Justin Wrobleski (pNERD 6.24) is trying to shake off a brutal stretch, having allowed nine home runs, leading to 16 runs allowed (15 earned) in 13 2/3 innings over his last three starts. Both tNERD scores sit near 9, well above the historical 95th percentile, with the Dodgers' scorching offense and the Brewers' elite bullpen and baserunning giving this game top-shelf team quality on both sides. With Ohtani stepping in against Misiorowski's heater and a first-place showdown on the line, this is appointment viewing.

San Diego riding a six-game winning streak into a game with real wild-card stakes, while Cleveland limps in having dropped four straight at home — this one leans watchable mostly because of the Padres, not despite them. San Diego's 10.23 tNERD is among the best you'll see today, built on a shutdown bullpen, sturdy baserunning, and above-average defense, even though the lineup itself hasn't been hitting for much thump lately. Cleveland's 7.80 mark is buoyed less by star power than by scrappy fundamentals — solid baserunning, a young, cheap roster, and some positive regression looming given their negative luck figure — but a genuinely poor barrel rate keeps the offense capped, and reports have José Ramírez out of Friday's lineup. Joey Cantillo takes the mound with a respectable 5.54 pNERD, his above-average whiff rate and xFIP- in the mid-90s making him a legitimately interesting look, even if his control has wobbled. Both the Nationals and Mets are also-rans this year, but this game still has more juice than the standings suggest, thanks to a lineup that leads the league in power and a Mets team quietly riding a bit of a patchwork pitching renaissance. Washington's offense is the story here — the Nationals have hit 177 total home runs to lead the NL, and that pop plus solid baserunning drives their tNERD to a strong 9.26, comfortably above both the historic and today's-game averages. Summary

Two last-place NL West clubs playing out the string, with Logan Webb as the lone reason to tune in. Both the Rockies and Giants are buried near the bottom of the division, and the standings tell the story here: San Francisco enters the matchup at 50-71, while Colorado is 48-73. The Giants get a boost from a strong recent Webb outing — he gave up one earned run and allowed four hits in eight innings pitched against the Detroit Tigers on Sunday — and his solid xFIP- of 89 backs up that eye test, making him comfortably the best thing on the mound today. Lorenzen, by contrast, has been a steady disappointment; he is 3-10 with a 6.83 ERA and 81 strikeouts in 112 2/3 innings pitched, and his peripherals (weak swinging-strike and strike rates) mostly back up that ugly line, though positive luck suggests some slight regression toward respectability is fair to expect. Both offenses are middling-to-poor, and neither bullpen stands out. With a gNERD of 6.54 — below both the historical and today's averages — this is a game for Webb completionists only, not casual viewers.
